findings.text: Resource accounting distinguishes live use, configured ceiling, observed peak and breach tally, each tracked separately for normal and reserved charges, giving eight selector values.

Node breakdown reporting supports two hierarchy modes. Legacy mode emits a direct summed total with per node values followed by a hierarchical total with per node subtree aggregates. Unified mode emits only the hierarchical view. Hierarchical totals come from the group counter while per node hierarchical values aggregate descendant groups.

Integer reads dispatch on the file selector to return live counter value, configured ceiling, observed peak or breach tally. Byte oriented results are scaled by the base page size while breach tallies are returned unscaled. Unknown selectors are treated as fatal.

Textual unified reads show live use numerically in bytes and show ceilings symbolically when at the rounded down maximum, otherwise numerically in bytes. A reserved selector variant selects the reserve counter rather than the normal counter.
Updates to normal and reserved ceilings are serialized by a dedicated limit mutex held across the ceiling change.

Ceiling writes reject the root group, normalize surrounding whitespace, parse the input against a caller supplied unlimited token, align the request down to the granularity of the selected huge page size, then apply it to the normal or reserved counter under the limit mutex and report full consumption on success.
Two write wrappers provide hierarchy specific unlimited tokens, one for legacy mode and one for unified mode, sharing a common implementation.
Reset writes clear observed peaks or zero breach tallies according to the file selector, rejecting selectors that are not resettable.
Event reporting exposes a single breach count with separate aggregate and local only views selected by distinct show routines sharing a common helper.
Unified control table defines seven entries binding show and write handlers, selector values and event file offsets, with every entry excluded from the root group.
Legacy control table defines nine entries binding integer read, write and reset handlers with selector values and no root exclusion flag in the fragments shown.
Unified hierarchy exposes files named max, rsvd.max, current, rsvd.current, events, events.local and numa_stat.
Legacy hierarchy exposes files named limit_in_bytes, rsvd.limit_in_bytes, usage_in_bytes, rsvd.usage_in_bytes, max_usage_in_bytes, rsvd.max_usage_in_bytes, failcnt, rsvd.failcnt and numa_stat.
The huge page control subsystem provides allocation, offline and free operations and points both unified and legacy type lists at a shared terminator table.

Contiguous reservation state uses per node area handles, per node byte sizes and per node percentages, plus global size, global percentage and an exclusive use flag, with early boot lifetimes for inputs and post init protection for established areas.
Node memory sizing has two build variants, one summing only memory regions homed on the queried node and one returning total physical memory regardless of node.

Reservation size boot option accepts either a list of node qualified extents separated by commas or a single global extent. Each extent is a size or a percentage with range validation. Node qualified input clears any global input and global input clears per node inputs. Parsing stops at the first malformed element.
Exclusive use boot option is interpreted as a boolean value.
Architecture alignment order for contiguous reservation is a weak hook defaulting to zero to indicate lack of support.

Reservation proceeds from percentage to byte conversion through gigantic granularity alignment and validation, then per node declaration. Global requests are spread across boot nodes with upward rounding. Each declaration is zone validated and accumulated. Global size is cleared when nothing could be reserved.
Zone containment validation in the configuration shown reports failure unconditionally.
Two headers define conventional inclusion guards to prevent multiple inclusion.

Allowed node helpers move to the next permitted node and normalize an impermissible start node to the next permissible one, asserting that results stay within range and that an allowed set is supplied.
Allocation and freeing cursors both advance round robin within the allowed set, one using caller held position storage and the other using per size state.
A global integer knob controls whether gigantic pages are movable.
Numeric vector sysctl handling duplicates the control descriptor and redirects the duplicate data pointer to a caller temporary to avoid races with the generic handler.

Pool size controls operate on the default huge page size, reject unsupported platforms, edit through a temporary and commit through a common store on write. Plain and policy aware variants differ only in a boolean selecting memory policy obedience.
Overcommit control edits a temporary copy of the default size allowance, rejects writes for gigantic sizes lacking runtime support, and commits the new value under interrupt safe spin protection.
System control names include nr_hugepages, nr_hugepages_mempolicy on NUMA builds, hugetlb_shm_group, nr_overcommit_hugepages and movable_gigantic_pages on migration builds, each with mode 0644.
System file attribute helpers generate read only, write only and read write attributes. A global object plus a per size object array anchor the hierarchy.
Object to state lookup scans global per size objects first and reports no specific node on a hit, otherwise delegating to node specific lookup.
NUMA aware object lookup scans per node per size objects and returns the owning size with its node, treating absence as fatal.
The non NUMA object lookup variant always faults, reports an invalid node identifier when requested and returns null.
Hierarchical node aggregation holds a read side critical section while walking descendant groups and uses single copy atomic reads for per node usage snapshots.
Overcommit value commits are protected by an interrupt disabling global spin lock.
Unrecognized selectors in integer and textual limit reads are treated as fatal programming errors rather than returning an error.
Unlimited ceiling input is "-1" in legacy mode and "max" in unified mode, and unified ceiling display shows "max" when at the effective maximum.

Invalid reservation inputs and failures are dropped with warnings, including out of range percentages and node identifiers, non multiple sizes, zero rounding, unsupported architecture order, declaration errors and zone spanning areas.
